summary: Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who held posts as Professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).
Shubhangni Gupta is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied as a doctoral student at Stanford University (attested 2026), where she was a PhD candidate in 2019.

Shuddhatam Prakash Jain is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar educated at multiple institutions, including Rajasthan and Sampurnanand Sanskrit Universities. He held posts at Central Sanskrit University, Vasundhara Teacher's Training College, Mangalayatan University, Ghanaram Hariram College, and Somaiya Vidyavihar University.

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University as an assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1984, 2014), and served as acting head of Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Zhejiang University, Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, and several Lyon and Paris academies. He taught at CAFA and the National Academy of Art, and long directed the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato (1919–2008) worked in Japanology, history, archaeology, and philosophy after studying at the University of Tokyo and University of Paris. He held academic appointments at UBC, Free University of Berlin, Sophia University, Brown University, Collège de France, and Ritsumeikan University.
Shuichi Maida (1906–1967) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Haya Akegarasu.

Shuichi Nara (born 1961), a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at Keio University. As of 2026, he is attested as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and lecturer at Chuo University.

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held research and lecturing posts at Ryukoku University (attested 2003), Bukkyo University (attested 2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2006), and Musashino University (attested 2006).

Shujiro Shimada (1907–1994) was a scholar of Japanology, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from approximately 1928 to 1931 and held a post at Princeton University around 1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and at Kyoto University, later serving on the faculty at Shinshu University, where he was Professor of Ethics (attested 2010).

Shuken Ito (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at Komazawa University. He spent his career there, advancing from assistant in 1973 to professor in 1991, and was a visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University in 1998.

Shuman Chen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen earned a PhD at Northwestern University, studying under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn, and also studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang (1893–1988) worked in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Shuntian Middle School, he joined Peking University's philosophy department in 1917, and later founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and the China Democratic League.

Shumpei Ueyama (1921–2012) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and history. After studying at Kyoto University, he became an associate professor and professor there, later serving as president of Kyoto City University of Arts and director of the Kyoto National Museum.
Shun Hidaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who was an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Shun'ei Hirai (born 1930) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, and spent his career at Komazawa University as a lecturer, professor, vice president, and professor emeritus.
Shun'ei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. Mori held positions at Ryukoku University (attested 1990) and Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).
Shunei Tsuboi (1923–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested in 1963 and 1972).

Shunji Hosaka (born 1956) is a religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He held posts at Reitaku University and Chuo University, and lectures at ICPBS, IIBS, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
